title: Reception Third Term
overview: Audit Correction Notice Version 1.1 preserves the approved Reception Third Term curriculum and corrects one legal-status wording issue identified during the Volume III audit: the Early Learning Goals are statutory within England's EYFS system, while AMES adopts them in Nigeria as an end-of-Reception reference framework for its British-system programme. No termly progression has been changed. 1. Third-Term Curriculum Intent Reception Third Term completes the Angel Montessori Early Years journey. First Term: SETTLE -> SECURE -> DECODE -> REPRESENT -> REASON. Second Term: DEEPEN -> READ -> COMPOSE -> INVESTIGATE -> APPLY. Third Term: FLUENCY -> INDEPENDENCE -> CONNECTION -> REFLECTION -> TRANSITION. The term continues Reception teaching properly while preparing children developmentally, academically, socially and emotionally for Basic 1. RECEPTION DOES NOT END WHEN TRANSITION PREPARATION BEGINS. 2. Reception to Basic 1 Bridge Reception Development Transition Towards Basic 1 Listen and participate Sustain attention increasingly Rich oral language Explain ideas with greater precision Systematic phonics Apply phonics independently Decode matched texts Develop increasing fluency Discuss stories Demonstrate deeper comprehension Write simple sentences Compose increasingly independently Form letters Develop increasingly secure handwriting Understand quantities Apply number knowledge to problems Explore composition Reason about number relationships Investigate practically Record and explain findings Learn through provision Manage more structured learning Choose resources Organise resources independently Cooperate in play Collaborate on shared tasks Manage personal routines Take responsibility for self-management Seek adult support Attempt, evaluate and seek help appropriately Transition principle: PREPARE THE CHILD FOR BASIC 1 - DO NOT TURN RECEPTION INTO BASIC 1. 3. Third-Term Curriculum Map Week 1 - Growing and Changing Deepen understanding that living things and people change over time. Use growth, change, mature, younger, older, past, present, future, before and after; observe and compare change; measure and represent observations. Character: Gratitude and Patience. Week 2 - Life Cycles Develop understanding of life cycles through observation, books, models and investigation; observe, sequence, compare, predict and explain. Character: Wonder and Care. Week 3 - Our Environment Understand relationships between people and environment through plants, animals, water, soil, weather, waste, cleanliness, reuse and resource care, beginning with school, home and Owo. KNOWLEDGE -> CARE -> RESPONSIBLE ACTION. Character: Stewardship. Week 4 - Nigeria - Our Country Deepen knowledge of Nigeria, Owo, flag, selected national symbols, people, occupations, cities/communities, languages, foods, music, clothing, landscapes and diversity. Character: Identity, Respect and Gratitude. Week 5 - Africa and Our Wider World Develop OWO -> ONDO STATE -> NIGERIA -> AFRICA -> WORLD using globes, maps, photographs, books, stories and purposeful digital resources; represent African life accurately and diversely. Character: Respect and Curiosity. Week 6 - Consolidation / Calendar Flexibility Review phonics, reading, comprehension, writing, handwriting, number, reasoning, communication, PSED, physical development, Understanding the World, Expressive Arts and Practical Life. INTERVENE WHILE THERE IS STILL TIME TO MAKE A DIFFERENCE. Week 7 - Becoming Fluent Readers Continue adopted SSP and cumulative review; matched decodables support accuracy, automaticity, phrasing and meaning; develop comprehension while adults continue rich read-aloud literature. THE CHILD'S DECODING LEVEL MUST NEVER BECOME THE LIMIT OF THE CHILD'S LITERARY EXPERIENCE. Week 8 - Becoming Independent Writers Use THINK -> SAY -> REHEARSE -> SEGMENT -> WRITE -> READ BACK -> IMPROVE; increasingly write labels, captions, messages, lists, sentences, story sequences, information and personal experiences. Week 9 - Mathematical Problem-Solvers Apply subitising, cardinality, composition, comparison, number relationships, one more/one fewer, doubling, sharing, grouping and appropriate odd/even patterns through meaningful problems and representations. Week 10 - Design, Build, Test, Improve Integrate science, mathematics, language, creativity and collaboration through NOTICE -> IMAGINE -> PLAN -> BUILD -> TEST -> IMPROVE -> EXPLAIN. Character: Creativity, Cooperation and Perseverance. Week 11 - Looking Back at Reception Reflect through meaningful portfolios and revisit learning; identify strengths, secure/developing learning, support needs and successful strategies. Character: Gratitude and Reflection. Week 12 - Getting Ready for Basic 1 Prepare practically and emotionally through familiarisation, organisation, self-care, resource management, listening, task initiation, persistence, completion, independent work, collaboration and clarification. CONFIDENCE COMES FROM FAMILIARITY, NOT PRESSURE. Week 13 - Celebration and Moving Forward Celebrate the whole child and completion of AMES Early Years. GRADUATION IS A CELEBRATION - NOT AN ACADEMIC RANKING CEREMONY. 4. End-of-Reception EYFS Position The Early Learning Goals (ELGs) are the statutory end-of-Reception assessment expectations within England's EYFS system. Angel Montessori School operates in Nigeria; they are therefore not Nigerian statutory requirements. AMES adopts the ELGs as its end-of-Reception reference framework within its British-system Early Years programme. The reference covers Communication & Language (Listening, Attention and Understanding; Speaking); PSED (Self-Regulation; Managing Self; Building Relationships); Physical Development (Gross Motor; Fine Motor); Literacy (Comprehension; Word Reading; Writing); Mathematics (Number; Numerical Patterns); Understanding the World (Past and Present; People, Culture and Communities; Natural World); and Expressive Arts & Design (Creating with Materials; Being Imaginative and Expressive). 5. Critical AMES ELG Principle The ELGs are end-of-Reception assessment expectations, not a checklist for narrowing the curriculum. AMES maintains RICH CURRICULUM FIRST -> ASSESSMENT OF LEARNING SECOND, including shape, space, measure, technology, Practical Life, outdoors, Christian character, Nigerian identity, creative exploration and rich literature. 6. End-of-Reception Phonics Position Progress through the adopted systematic synthetic phonics programme according to its Reception sequence. Transition records specify secure grapheme-phoneme correspondences, blending, segmenting, approach to unfamiliar decodable words, matched-book fluency and gaps requiring continued support. 7. End-of-Reception Reading Develop increasingly strong foundations in decoding, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension, book enjoyment, story knowledge, information texts and discussion. READING IS DECODING + LANGUAGE + MEANING + THINKING + ENJOYMENT. 8. End-of-Reception Writing Integrate ideas, oral language, sentence composition, phonics, spelling, letter formation, spacing and rereading through real purposes. Goal: MEANINGFUL, INCREASINGLY INDEPENDENT AND INCREASINGLY ACCURATE WRITING. 9. End-of-Reception Mathematics Deepen subitising, cardinality, composition, comparison, numerical patterns, reasoning, problem-solving and representation, alongside rich shape, space, measure, position, pattern, construction, capacity, length, height, weight and time. NUMERACY IS MORE THAN RECITING NUMBER NAMES. 10. Communication and Language Consider whether children increasingly listen attentively, follow increasingly complex instructions, respond appropriately, ask questions, explain, retell, use new vocabulary, sustain conversation, communicate needs and express ideas clearly enough to be understood. 11. PSED and Self-Regulation Basic 1 readiness includes increasing ability to separate confidently, manage emotions, recover from disappointment, wait, take turns, cooperate, maintain friendships, resolve simple conflict, seek help, persist, follow expectations and manage personal needs. SELF-REGULATION IS NOT SILENT COMPLIANCE. 12. Physical Development Transition information includes gross-motor coordination, balance, movement, fine-motor control, pencil use, cutting, manipulation, self-care and physical access needs. 13. Practical Life - End of Reception Third Term reaches: I AM READY TO TAKE GREATER RESPONSIBILITY. Children increasingly manage self, belongings, resources, workspace, hygiene, simple responsibilities, help-seeking, completion and environmental care. 14. Continuous Provision Until the End Do not dismantle continuous provision after assessment. Reception remains Early Years until the end of the programme. 15. Transition Principle PREPARE THE CHILD FOR BASIC 1 - DO NOT TURN RECEPTION INTO BASIC 1. Document Control Document Code: AMES-003-R-T3 Version: 1.1 Status: APPROVED CONTENT - AUDIT CORRECTED Correction: EYFS/ELG England-versus-Nigeria legal-status wording clarified; curriculum progression retained. Academic Session: 2026/2027
